persona.role: MBA student with engineering and IT experience

sent_to_model:
I'm writing an email to Vince, who I worked for over the summer, because I'm getting close to finishing my MBA and could use his advice. I'm having trouble getting employers to appreciate the combination of finance and technical skills I bring. I need more than help locating openings; I'd like his thoughts on how to distinguish myself from the other MBA candidates. Could you help me ask for his advice and any company leads he might have? I also want him to know I'm willing to relocate anywhere in the U.S. and that I appreciated working with him and the team.

- Recipient: Vince, former summer supervisor.
- Undergraduate engineering education at Cornell University.
- Open to relocating anywhere within the U.S.
- Graduating in May; MBA from Rice, finance concentration.
- Also an IT specialist.
- Interested in companies of any size.
- Economy is difficult for job seekers.
- Available for questions by telephone or email whenever needed.
- Mike Roberts praised my three months with the weather group: greater accomplishment than other MBAs managed over a full year.
- Summer work involved implementing models as program code; could do this rapidly and dependably.
- Interviewers tend to seek one specialty rather than my full combination of abilities.
- Enjoyed the summer job with Vince; felt the team worked well together.
- Frustrated by difficulty communicating why I can contribute more effectively than classmates.
- Consider myself strongest in the class in finance, statistics and IT; cannot comfortably make that claim on a resume.
- Technical training probably explains the strong summer performance.
- Having several strengths also complicates finding a suitable role.
- Advice on standing out among MBA classmates during the job search.
- Introductions or leads to employers interested in the combined skill set.
- A role using all my skills, with an opportunity to demonstrate good work and early results.
- Vince to know his time and suggestions are appreciated.

(About me: MBA student with engineering and IT experience. Length: it should come to roughly 250-400 words.)

must_cover: Ask Vince for advice on distinguishing the writer from other MBA candidates.
Describe the difficulty of finding employers who value the combined finance and technical skills.
Request company leads and communicate willingness to relocate anywhere in the U.S.
Express appreciation for Vince and the experience working with his team.
